title: How Anthropic Redesigned Source Control for AI-Driven Development
gist: Anthropic migrated its monorepo from Git to Scion, a server-side, content-addressed source control system with tiered caches, after AI-driven daily merged changes rose from ~2,500 in May to over 30,000 in September 2026 and CI hit ~25 million checkouts a day. Anthropic reports a 200x smaller infrastructure footprint and ~100x faster checkouts, but says Scion is bespoke and not a general Git replacement.

insights.claim: Daily merged changes in Anthropic's monorepo rose from around 2,500 in May 2026 to more than 30,000 in September 2026, a roughly 12x increase in four months.
insights.so_what: Quantifies how agentic coding is multiplying software output, stressing dev infrastructure.
insights.quote: daily merged changes rose from around 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Anthropic's CI systems perform about 25 million checkouts daily against a monorepo with nearly 100 GB of main-branch history and a compressed working copy over 25 GB.
insights.so_what: Agent and CI workloads create a new scale tier for source control and CI vendors.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Standard Git scaling techniques (shallow clones, sparse checkouts, promisor remotes, snapshots, several hundred Git mirrors) became harder to operate as merge rates increased.
insights.so_what: Git-based platforms may face pressure to re-architect for agent-scale workloads.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Scion moves commits, merges, rebases, history and blame to the server, with clients holding bounded caches and virtualised checkouts that materialise files on demand, trading offline independence for less local data and shared infrastructure.
insights.so_what: Signals a shift from distributed toward centralised, API-first source control for AI workloads.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Scion checkouts flow through node-local daemons, regional caches and authoritative servers backed by Spanner and cloud storage, with enforced tier ordering so a regional cache failure cannot overwhelm the authoritative servers.
insights.so_what: Anthropic relies on Google Cloud infrastructure (Spanner) for core developer tooling.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Anthropic reports cache-hit rates above 99% at each tier, an infrastructure CPU and memory footprint 200 times smaller than its previous Git mirrors, and checkout speedups of two orders of magnitude for CI and research jobs.
insights.so_what: Large infra cost savings show where AI-native dev tooling can create value; results are company-reported.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Anthropic credited Meta's Mononoke and its Bonsai data model with pioneering many of Scion's techniques, and Scion goes further than Uber's GitFarm by changing the underlying data model.
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler-grade monorepo tooling is diffusing to AI labs.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Anthropic cautions that Scion is not a general-purpose Git replacement because it requires its own code-review, code-search and CI systems, and recommends bringing ideas like server-side APIs and better fetch protocols into existing Git platforms.
insights.so_what: Opportunity for GitHub/GitLab-style platforms to add agent-scale server-side APIs rather than be displaced.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller

insights.claim: Architects should reconsider where work happens as workloads change, since repository queries need not require local checkouts, though server dependence and heavy integration are the costs.
insights.so_what: Agent workloads favour centralised, cache-heavy infrastructure designs.
insights.speaker: Eran Stiller
